Done. Since the workspace contained only the problem spec (no codebase to patch), I diagnosed the root cause, implemented the fix as a complete software-rasterizer core, and verified it numerically with an independent ground truth (Möller–Trumbore ray-triangle intersection, so the fix and truth can't share a bug).

## Deliverables

- **`/workspace/SOLUTION.md`** — the solution writeup: title, root-cause analysis, exact fix (canonical formulas, full reference implementation, WebGL/GLSL translation notes), and the verification section with the real measured numbers.
- **`/workspace/solution/reference.js`** — runnable fixed pipeline (Node ≥ 20, zero deps).
- **`/workspace/solution/verify.js`** — verification harness; run with `cd solution && node verify.js` (exit 0, deterministic).

## Root cause (one bug, three symptoms)

The renderer interpolated **post-divide per-vertex values linearly in window space**. Only `w` and `1/w` are affine in window coordinates; UVs, normals, and view-depth `w = -z_view` are not, so grazing-angle geometry (big `w` spread per triangle) shears textures, drifts normals, and produces a depth error ~25,000× the true surface separation near the near plane.

## The fix (one stroke)

Per fragment, with window barycentrics λ:

```
invW  = Σλᵢ/wᵢ                            (exact, linear in window space)
attr  = (Σλᵢ·aᵢ/wᵢ) / invW                (perspective-correct)
depth = (1/near − invW)/(1/near − 1/far)  (w-buffer: perspective-consistent space)
```

## Verified results

| Test | Buggy | Fixed |
|---|---|---|
| Grazing ground quad UV shear | max error **0.63** UV units | ≤ 2.1e-14 |
| Normal drift, camera 2→0.25 above surface | mean 9.5° → 21.5° (max 24°→33°) | ≤ 1.7e-6° |
| Depth error, near=0.01, 1e-4 separation | up to **2.53** units | ≤ 1.6e-12 |
| 24-bit depth-buffer winner test | **19.1%** wrong pixels | **0%** |

A bonus finding documented in §2.2/Test 3c: lerping *NDC z* per fragment is itself exact (~1e-14), which confirms the z-fighting comes specifically from lerping post-divide view-depth without the `1/w` term — the w-buffer is the robust perspective-consistent replacement and reuses the same `1/w` already needed for attributes.

signatures.description: A WebGL renderer interpolates per-vertex UV and normal attributes linearly in window space instead of weighting by 1/w, so textured quads shear and lighting normals drift as the camera approaches, while depth is stored post-divide without the perspective term, causing near-plane z-fighting. Rewrite the pipeline to interpolate attribute/w and 1/w across each triangle and recover attributes per fragment, keeping the depth value in a perspective-consistent space. Validate with a ground-plane texture viewed at grazing angle and a depth-stress scene whose near plane is 0.01.
